Target company: Advanced Micro Devices (AMD). AMD designs computing and graphics processors, including Ryzen, EPYC and Radeon products, serving PC, data-center, gaming and embedded markets.

Focal announcement: AMD Instinct MI300X Accelerators Available on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure for Demanding AI Applications.

Decision cutoff: 2024-09-26T23:59:59-04:00. Use only information available before this cutoff.

Source: AMD Instinct MI300X Accelerators Available on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure for Demanding AI Applications. Published date: 2024-09-26. URL: https://ir.amd.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1217/amd-instinct-mi300x-accelerators-available-on-oracle-cloud-infrastructure-for-demanding-ai-applications.

Condensed source passage, selected from the supplied excerpt; other details are omitted: — Customers including Fireworks AI are powering their AI inference and training workload s with new OCI Compute instances -- SANTA CLARA, Calif., Sept. 26, 2024 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) today announced that Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) has chosen AMD Instinct™ MI300X accelerators with ROCm™ open software to power its newest OCI Compute Supercluster instance called BM.GPU.MI300X.8. For AI models that can comprise hundreds of billions of parameters, the OCI Supercluster with AMD MI300X supports up to 16,384 GPUs in a single cluster by harnessing the same ultrafast network fabric technology used by other accelerators on OCI. “The inference capabilities of AMD Instinct MI300X accelerators add to OCI’s extensive selection of high-performance bare metal instances to remove the overhead of virtualized compute commonly used for AI infrastructure,” said Donald Lu, senior vice president, software development, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. "The amount of memory capacity available on the AMD Instinct MI300X and ROCm open software allows us to scale services to our customers as models continue to grow."
